## Installation
### Requirements

1. **`agy` installed**: `irm https://antigravity.google/cli/install.ps1 | iex`
(Windows). The plugin

locates it automatically (PATH → `AGY_BIN` →
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\agy\bin` → `~/.local/bin` → `~/.gemini

/bin` → `~/go/bin`).
2. **`agy` logged in once**: run `agy` in a terminal and complete the
sign-in.

If a run hits "authentication required", the plugin pops the
interactive login window automatically.

3. **DeepSeekRuntime** with the standard web profile (it ships
`dsh-subagent`, `dsh-subprocess`, `d
sh-tools`, `dsh-jobs`).

## Usage

The model calls the tools automatically when you ask for it; you can also
prompt it explicitly:
| Surface | Name | What it does |
| task / follow-up | `antigravity` | pass `prompt` for a fresh conversation, or `task` to continue o

ne (full context carries over); both work with `background: true` |
| follow-up (foreground) | `anti
gravity_followup` | foreground-only shortcut for `antigravity({ task, prompt })`; use the latter for

`background` / `model` / `effort` / `dirs` |
| list | `antigravity_tasks` | list running tasks + re

cent finished tasks; `task` keys survive DSH restarts |
| cancel | `antigravity_cancel` | stop a run

ning task by its `task` key (agy process tree terminated) |
| login | `antigravity_login` | pop the
interactive agy login window (also opens automatically on auth failures) |

Any call may also override `model` (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-6`) and `effort`
(`low` / `medium` / `high

` / `xhigh` / `max`) for that run only, without
touching the global configuration.
Example prompts:

> "Use agy to rewrite the README of `D:\projects\my-project` and list the changes."
>
> "Let antigra

vity rework this project's landing page — use claude-sonnet-4-6 at max effort."
>
> "用 antigravity 优
化这个项目的页面" *(in a Chinese session)*
### Sidebar panel

The sidebar footer carries an **Antigravity Manager** button: `●N` is the number of running jobs
and

the percentage is the five-hour quota left for the **model family of the
configured model** (hover

for the reset time). Clicking it opens the
**Antigravity Manager** tab in the right sidebar:

- **Four quota cards**, taken straight from `agy --print "/usage"`: Gemini
Models / Claude and GPT m

odels × five-hour / weekly, each with its reset time.
One probe takes ~10 seconds, so the result is

cached briefly
(single-flight — many open panes still spawn one agy); the card's refresh
button forc

es a new probe, and the cards say **when** the numbers were read —
the probe is slow, and stale numb

ers should be obvious at a glance.
- **Token spend card**, for estimating what a Pro plan actually g

ives you: it
adds up every agy conversation on the machine, not just the ones this plugin
ran — the

Antigravity IDE's store
(`~/.gemini/antigravity/brain`) spends the same account quota, and leaving i

t
out under-counts a normal day by roughly 4x. The headline is the **total
[该节后续省略]
## How it works (short version)

Each task spawns a fresh `agy -p <task>` process in the session workspace
and returns the final answ

er. Runs use `--output-format json`, whose reply
carries agy's `conversation_id`; the plugin records

it in a durable registry
(`~/.dsh/agy-conversations.json`), and `antigravity({ task })` resumes the

same conversation via `--conversation <id>`. Background runs use
`stream-json` for live progress an

d register with DSH's jobs system
(`job_output` / `job_kill`). The job's owner is the calling sessio

n, so a
settled job **wakes** it — the model is told not to poll. A local watchdog terminates hung r

uns, and all
timeouts interrupt: nothing ever waits forever.
